<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Models and meaning</p><h1>Netflix trends</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>13 Jun 2023</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>What does a catalogue say when you stop looking at the titles one by one? This notebook explores Netflix title data through text analysis and visualization.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>Can simple representations of title language reveal useful patterns without pretending to explain the whole catalogue?</p><h2>What the text can do</h2><p>Token counts, word associations, and vector views make the language inspectable. They also remind us that the text of a title is not the same thing as the audience, the story, or the platform's recommendation system.</p><p>Text is a map. It is not the territory with subtitles.</p></article></main>
